dailyInsight.headline: Test an AUTO-mode denial with one exact retry, not a broader exception
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's public source change gives a classifier-blocked action one path back to a person: repeat the same tool call from the same working directory and receive a manual review. In a disposable source checkout, operators can test that narrow handoff without treating a policy block as permission to search for an equivalent workaround.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The change fingerprints the tool name, canonicalized parameters, and working directory. A classifier block stores that fingerprint; only a matching next call falls into manual confirmation, consumes the retry before display, and suppresses persistent approval. Changed arguments or a changed directory are reclassified, while destructive commands retain their explicit-approval guard.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A safety denial is useful only if the person responsible for the work can understand what is being decided. Binding the review to one identifiable action preserves human control without turning a single false positive into a broad exception for nearby commands.

actions.audience: Qwen Code source-build operators and builders of comparable AUTO-mode agents
actions.label: Run an exact-retry boundary check
actions.instruction: In a disposable checkout, run the focused AUTO-mode tests or arrange a known non-destructive policy block. Retry the identical call from the same directory and confirm one manual review appears without persistent approval; then alter an argument and verify that it is reclassified. Do not use destructive command examples.

receipts.title: fix(core): allow manual retry after auto mode blocks (#11025)
receipts.supports: The public review record identifies the bounded recovery change and makes its scope inspectable alongside the merged implementation.

receipts.title: fix(core): allow manual retry after auto mode blocks (#11025)
receipts.supports: The merged source adds an action fingerprint based on tool, canonical parameters, and working directory, then limits the manual fallback to that matching action.

receipts.title: AUTO-mode retry fingerprint and destructive-command guard tests
receipts.supports: The public tests check canonical-argument matching within one working directory and preserve the separate destructive-command guard rather than offering its retry path.

confidence.basis: The fresh public PR, merged implementation, and focused tests agree on a narrow one-shot fallback, but they do not establish live classifier behavior or release inclusion.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts establish intended source and regression-test behavior only. They do not prove a released build contains the change, that a live classifier makes consistent decisions, or that every UI and ACP path renders the review identically.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if a public test or issue shows changed arguments or directories inheriting the retry, persistent approval appearing in the fallback, or destructive actions receiving the same retry invitation.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a tagged release and public runtime evidence showing an operator can distinguish the exact reviewed action from a materially changed follow-up command.
